restDay.label: Rest day
restDay.headline: Not a day off — a day the muscle actually grows.
restDay.note: Growth happens between sessions, not during them. Walking is fine and good. Everything else on this list still counts, so a rest day never breaks the streak.

home.label: Bodyweight
home.note: No equipment. Progression is by variation and tempo instead of weight: when you hit the top of the rep range on every set, move up a rung and drop back to the bottom of the range. Currently weighted towards upper body, with glutes twice a week — general leg work is parked until the upper body catches up.

sessions.label: Upper — Push
sessions.headline: Chest and triceps. Pike push-ups are the closest thing to shoulder work you have.

items.detail: Elbows about 45° from your body, not flared. Full range — chest to the floor.
Hips high, head travels toward the floor between your hands. The best delt work available without weights — treat it as the priority movement of this session.
Two stable chairs or the edge of a sofa. Shoulders down, don't sink into the shrug.
Hands together under the chest. Triceps.

sessions.label: Back, Glutes & Core
sessions.headline: The general leg work is gone — upper body and glutes are the priority now. Glutes come early, while you're fresh.

ladder: Reverse snow angel, paused at the top
items.detail: Face down, arms out on the floor, palms up. Sweep them from beside your hips up over your head and back, keeping hands lifted the whole time. Burns the mid-back and rear delts.

ladder: Glute bridge, paused at the top
items.detail: Heels close to your backside, drive through them and squeeze hard at the top for a full second. This is the main glute builder — a six-rung ladder, so it keeps getting harder without any weight.
Second back exposure of the week. Frequency is what you have instead of load.

ladder: Side-lying leg raise, paused at the top
items.detail: Hits the side of the glute — that's the part that adds shape rather than just size. Toes pointed slightly down, not up.
Lower back pressed flat into the floor the whole time.
Builds the waist taper from the side.

sessions.label: Upper — Pull
sessions.headline: The hardest session to do without a bar. Inverted rows are the whole game here.

ladder: Prone pull-down, paused at the bottom
items.detail: Face down, chest and arms lifted off the floor and kept there for the whole set. Row: arms out in a T, pull your elbows back to your ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together, reach back out. Pull-down: same movement, but start with your arms straight overhead — longer arm, so it's harder. Squeeze deliberately; the only resistance you have is your own arms against gravity, so how hard you pull is the load.
Face down, arms and legs lifted, flutter opposite arm and leg. Lower back and the whole rear chain.
Face down, arms making a Y then T then W. Rear delts and mid-back — this is genuinely useful equipment-free work and it protects your shoulders for the gym later.

ladder: Single-leg Romanian deadlift, paused at the bottom
items.detail: Second glute session of the week, and a different angle from the bridge — this one stretches the glute under load instead of squeezing it short. Push your hips back, keep a soft knee, feel it in the back of the leg.
Lower back and spinal erectors.

sessions.label: Arms & shoulders
sessions.headline: Second shoulder exposure of the week. Do these when you're fresh, not tacked on tired.

items.detail: Second exposure this week. Frequency is what you have instead of load.
Triceps.
Rear and medial delts. Slow — there's no weight, so time under tension is all you've got.

Stand side-on, press the back of your hand into the wall as if raising the arm, and hold. Being straight with you: this is a poor substitute for a loaded lateral raise and won't build much width. It's here to keep the movement pattern alive until you have dumbbells.

gym.label: Gym
gym.note: Parked until you have a subscription. Switch by setting activeProgram to "gym" — nothing else needs rewriting.

sessions.label: Upper — Push
sessions.headline: Lateral raises are the priority movement of the whole plan.

items.detail: Barbell or dumbbell. Your priority press.
The single biggest visual driver. Slow, no swinging.

sessions.label: Lower
sessions.headline: Keep it honest but don't let it eat your upper-body recovery.

items.detail: Barbell or hack.

sessions.label: Upper — Pull
sessions.headline: Back width is the other half of the V-taper.

items.detail: Back width = V-taper.

items.text: Lateral raise, machine or leaning cable · 4×12–15
items.detail: Yes, again. Different angle.
Shoulder health and width.

sessions.label: Arms & delts
sessions.headline: The weak-point day. Third lateral raise exposure of the week.

items.detail: As prescribed.
As prescribed. Consistent time of day.

daily.title: Eat
daily.note: Protein is the non-negotiable — 1.8–2.2 g per kg per day. Four anchors of 35–45 g beats trying to rescue the number at dinner. The failure mode isn't one light day, it's three in a row.

items.detail: Greek yoghurt or skyr + eggs, or a shake with milk.
Palm-and-a-half of chicken / fish / beef / tofu.
The one that usually rescues the day's total.
Pale straw, not clear. Creatine raises water needs slightly.
Only needed for the first 2–3 weeks, to calibrate. After that you'll know your portions by eye.
Any time of day. No loading phase needed.

daily.title: Care
daily.note: Minoxidil every evening, except on microneedling days — the skin needs about a day and a half to close up before anything goes on it again.

items.detail: Morning. Every 14 days. No minoxidil this evening — resume tomorrow evening.
Evening, on dry scalp. Hides itself automatically on microneedling days.
Short sleep measurably suppresses muscle gain and raises appetite. Consistent wake time matters more than consistent bedtime.
Tick it on the days you did. Costs XP on purpose — it changes sleep architecture, and sleep is the recovery lever the plan leans on hardest. A new id, so the old inverted ticks aren't read backwards.
Not in the hour after training — cold blunts the growth signal.
Every three days.

oneOffs.title: Setup
oneOffs.note: These disappear for good once ticked.

items.detail: Morning, unflexed, before eating. This is the one thing here that gets worse by waiting — a starting number taken next week isn't a starting number.
As real appointments, not intentions. Mon / Tue / Thu / Fri.
Enough floor to lie flat with your arms out, and two chairs that take your weight for dips. That's the whole kit list.
